title: Show separately Alert.read-authorized Incident origin in existing read-only Incident Detail
goal: Restore the canonical Incident upstream Alert triage source to the real Command Incident Detail, using two narrow server-authorized Command owners: relation owner and independent Alert.read owner. Show limited source provenance, no raw Signal/Event, no mutation or permission inheritance.
invariants: Command is owner of Incident and Alert; the Incident relationship is not an Alert.read grant. Incident.read is re-evaluated before any upstream link lookup.

IncidentAlertReferencesOwner returns only scoped relationship identifiers; independent IncidentAlertOwner must explicitly authorize perm.command.alert.read for principal, tenant, environment and each specific Alert, with null on denied.
An absent optional provider, absent relation or denied individual Alert produces a partial display, never a false assertion that source does not exist.
Every link and Alert owner response identity, source reference/version, bounded text and observation time must match authenticated Incident scope or fail the entire HTTP page before any HTML emits.
No raw Signal, Telemetry Event, Evidence, export, Case privilege transfer, mutation, extra route, paid dependency or production IAM.
security_properties: Revalidate principal, tenant, environment and Incident/Alert binding on every read; limit source references to 20; require distinct per-alert permissions; deny duplicate links.
Source failures, canceled context or mismatched identities produce generic HTTP 503 without raw source output; a denied Alert is not included even by ID or count.
Only strict HTML template autoescape and existing CSP/no-store/referrer protections used.

migration.rationale: Optional read-only HTML presentation; no storage or schema changes

rollback.strategy: Remove optional Alert owner interfaces and Incident Detail display, retain prior incident overview and linked Case navigation
verification: Original Incident Detail without Alert interfaces still renders Partial
Existing Command-only principal still cannot access Case or Alert

inputs: Existing source-authorized Incident Detail #209/#210 and Command owner, source-time context, immutable selected Incident
Canonical OBJ-ALERT and CMD-IWQ-006 read-only source requirement
outputs: One existing Incident Detail shows source Alert ID, source severity/status/disposition/provenance only if source owner independently allows Alert.read
Fail-closed bounded multi-source join with per-Alert isolation, nil/denied omissions and HTML escaping
Synthetic localhost Go HTTP tests exercising independent principal rights and regression behavior
acceptance_tests: Analyst who can read selected Incident and Alert sees actual source-origin fields in Detail; commander who can read Incident but not Alert sees no source ID or attributes
Wrong tenant/env/Incident link, duplicated/bad Alert IDs, malformed owner source/status/provenance/time or source failure abort without leaking prior authorized page content
One denied Alert among authorized references is omitted without disclosing its reference, while authorized Alert stays visible
Legacy owner without either optional interface remains functional, with explicit unavailable source message
Existing Work Queue, Incident Detail and same-origin host tests plus GitHub Actions on exact SHA pass; all obligatory security and statement coverage gates retained
definition_of_ready: K-OVERVIEW IMPLEMENTED on frozen reviewed PR #210 SHA 07900fa4c174f46a71a52debb3a93403faabd4c9; separate source read remains canonical but missing
Read-only Action Class 0 and OPEN-013 Class 2 excluded
definition_of_done: New independent owner source visible in actual localhost HTTP Incident Detail
Full Go tests/vet/race and engineering-kernel on exact SHA PASS
Independent L2 for new trust boundary before merge; no full Incident Detail or production acceptance claim

performance_budget.rationale: Bounded <=20 source link reads per already-authorized Incident and no Signal/Alert raw reads; synthetic performance only
metrics: <=20 owner-authorized referenced Alert lookups per request
